classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish horizontal dilations by comparing the amplitude and first positive zero of four sine graphs.

content.prompt: Which diagram shows the graph of $3\sin\left(\frac{x}{4}\right)$?

spec.description: Positive arch with maximum 3 at pi and zeros at 0 and 2pi. Ordinary curve, axes and labels use black; the origin O is omitted under house graph conventions.
Positive arch with maximum 3 at 2pi and zeros at 0 and 4pi. The horizontal coordinate is displayed in units of pi. Origin O omitted under house conventions.
Full sine cycle rising from the origin, crossing at 2pi and ending at 4pi, with extrema 3 and -3. Origin O omitted under house conventions.
Full sine cycle rising from the origin, crossing at pi and ending at 2pi, with extrema 3 and -3. Origin O omitted under house conventions.

answer.worked:
The amplitude is $3$ and the horizontal dilation factor is $4$, so the period is $8\pi$. The graph starts at $(0,0)$ and rises to $(2\pi,3)$, then returns to the axis at $(4\pi,0)$. Diagram B shows this first half-cycle.

Correct answer: B.
